en: Port town Milfe... Though on the frontier, it thrives as an independent city from maritime industry, mineral ore, and trade. I, having reached this destination, stopped upon entering the central plaza. The ship I'd taken partway to this city had run aground, so I continued overland on foot. With the relief of arrival, my body now feels a pleasant fatigue. Never normally one to tire, I welcomed the fresh sensation.
Feeling odd, I opened my shirt and looked inside.
I am unmistakably a man. Yet, there is a faint bulge that should not be on a man.

......
(I'd forgotten...
Shouldn't push myself too hard...)
I reflect on the bodily change my fatigue caused.
We have finally arrived, Master.

I closed my shirt and looked up, turning toward her.
A girl with a large bundle on her back looks up at me.
Her name is Shuri.
For various reasons, she's my servant,
brought along on this journey.
I took her in as a war orphan long ago.
Since then, she has worked in my home,
mainly tending to my daily needs.
Having served since childhood, she is especially
obedient, devoted, and capable among the servants.
But lately, maybe with age, she's grown more reserved,
keeping a step back from me...
and I find that a little lonely.
Is something the matter, Master?
No, it is nothing...
Shuri gazes at me. That somewhat anxious look has not changed one bit since I picked her up on the battlefield over a decade ago.
What shall we do now, Master?
Right... First, let's find an inn.
Yes, I hope there is a nice inn.
Yeah.

...!
As I scanned the plaza for an inn, a sharp killing intent suddenly pierced me.
I looked toward its source.
From a nearby eatery, a familiar figure appeared, shoulders squared in anger, striding toward me with great strides.
That is...
Still, we are three days behind schedule. I hope Levia is not too angry...
Shuri, who had never known killing intent, spoke without noticing. I answered with a sigh.
No, she is angry.
Huh?
Of course.
Ah, Ms. Levia!

Flanked by several soldiers, a woman in silver armor glares at me as if she would shoot me dead. She is General Levia, the only female knight commander in Lewinia, where I am currently a guest general, and an old acquaintance. I was supposed to meet her here three days ago, but...
Levia seems quite angry.
Celica! What have you been doing?
Levia closed in through the gap Shuri left.
The ship ran aground.
What?!
It didn't sink, but we walked here.
Shuri, is it true?

Yes, Ms. Levia.
Five days ago, the ship we were on ran aground.
Levia, who used to visit my mansion often and knows Shuri cannot tell a lie, nodded slowly as Shuri answered as if defending me.
If Shuri says so, it's true. But why did you walk? You could have hired a horse or carriage in any village along the way.

I hesitated for a moment...
I could have rented a carriage along the way,
but there was a reason I did not.
She is going to be angry...
My gaze met Shuri's puzzled eyes.
Even if I lied now, Shuri is so bad at lying
that it would only incur more of Levia's wrath.
Left with no choice, I decided to tell her the truth.
The scenery was nice...

For a moment, the air seemed to freeze.
Shuri cringed, bracing for Levia's anger
about to be unleashed on me.
...So you walked all the way here?
Yeah.
Levia's slender eyebrows bristled at my honest answer to her cold, piercing question.
What do you think this mission is?!
Levia's furious roar made the onlookers freeze.
To find the missing Princess Latina.
No, I mean the significance of this mission...
A princess, fourth in line, missing eighteen years. Even if we find her, she won't even serve as a political pawn...
You... This is a vital mission the Water Maiden has given us to clear our disgrace from the last great war.
Disgrace...

Not long ago, Lewinia, Levia's homeland and the country where I serve as a guest general, went to war with a neighboring nation. During that war, Levia's White Earth Dragon Knights and I fought a giant demon that was closing in on the capital from a direction apart from the main enemy force, a trump card. At great cost, we destroyed it. But those who saw only the demon's corpse, especially nobles who knew nothing of battle, were not like us who actually fought. They said Levia's command was poor because she lost so many soldiers. As for me, the wounds I suffered sapped my power, and I could not join later battles, so I was labeled worthless. The only one who gave us due recognition was the Water Maiden, the guardian deity of Lewinia and my ally.

Enshrined as a living god deep within the royal palace, she gave us this mission as an oracle, allowing us to recuperate and getting us out of the country while the postwar turmoil still simmered. But Levia seems not to have caught on to that, and she has thrown herself into it with excessive zeal. Even the intelligence that prompted this mission is dubious, a tale of a princess who went missing eighteen years ago being sighted in this city, her appearance unchanged since that time...
Even if the nobles do not acknowledge it, we destroyed a monster that could match an army. There is no disgrace to clear.
You're the one who defeated that monster.
I could not have defeated it alone.

Shut up! It was you who dealt the final blow.
I... I let my soldiers die for nothing...

Levia... Calling the lives lost in battle
a waste... I do not approve.
Ah... Sorry, forget I said that.
Yeah.

Perhaps embarrassed by her slip, her anger quickly
cooling, Levia turned away as if to hide her face.
For now, I will brief you on our findings. Come with me.
Where to?
Seeing Levia about to set off, I dodged Shuri, who, already laden with bags, was reaching for mine, and casually asked my question. The halting reply was unexpected.
I commandeered the lord's mansion... as our HQ.

Levia hates commandeering and looting above all.
And this city Milfe we came to under the pretext
of finding the princess is not Lewinian territory;
this could be taken as an act of aggression.
What happened?
A man stepped forward from beside the silent Levia.

Lord Celica, that matter was the doing
of common-born knights who admire General Levia.
Lord Ranzabu... The vice-commander of the knights under Levia. A man of constant dark rumors.
They must have wanted General Levia to have a comfortable environment in which to work, but...
Ranzabu shakes his head, as if troubled.
In the end, we paid the lord a fair sum to rent his mansion. But thanks to those common-born knights' thoughtlessness, we're now treated like invaders in this city.

Indeed, the locals watching us
do not have friendly eyes.
Enough, Lord Ranzabu. What is done is done...

Indeed, that is so.
I have spoken out of turn.
Please forgive me.

Ranzabu's words carry an unspoken blame toward Levia. A snake in the grass... I've heard he was promoted by nobles who dislike a woman being a general. He likely had a hand in the actions of those knights who supposedly admire her.
Ranzabu bowed politely to Levia, who had turned to face him, and then withdrew to his place behind her.
So, are we going to that mansion now?
Yeah.
Go on ahead. I'll find a place to stay.

If that is what you prefer...
No, I understand.

She showed a slightly dejected look,
and the next instant she turned and left briskly.
I understand what Levia wanted to say.
The mansion likely has rooms prepared for us...
But, I feel bad for Levia, I do not want
to get caught up in needless trouble.
And because Levia knows that too,
she probably left without a word.
Levia...

Levia, being a woman who holds the rank of general, always shoulders burdens she need not bear. Shuri, knowing nothing of the army's inner workings, cannot understand this, and it likely reminds her of her own powerlessness. As she watches Levia depart, her face is clouded with worry. ...It seems I will not be able to rest easily.
It's fine...
Master?
Yes, I suppose so.
Though I did not say much, my words seemed to wipe away Shuri's anxiety, if only a little.
Shuri turns toward me, waiting for my words.
Anyway, let's find an inn.

Ah, yes, of course.
Then I will find an inn. Master, you...
No need. Let's go into that place.
What?

Shuri turns, and her eyes fall on a sign that reads "Wild Bull's Hoof Inn". At first glance it seems a dining hall, but the size of the building suggests it serves as an inn as well. Seeing me start toward the inn, Shuri quickly steps ahead and opens the door. I pass her and step into the fragrant air of roasting meat.

"Welcome." A cheerful voice from a woman greeted us the moment we stepped inside. "Two of you? There are seats open over there." Looking around the nearly full shop, likely due to lunchtime, the woman, clearly a staff member, pointed to two empty seats at the counter.
Um, excuse me, is the master of this shop...
"Being called 'Master' makes me feel a bit ticklish, but I'm the one."
Ah, s-sorry!
"Heh, no need to apologize, really. So, you need something from me?"
Oh, no, I mean... any rooms free?
"So you are here for a room, then. Come to the counter."
Yes.
When we got to the empty seats at the counter, the shopkeeper, having circled behind it, pulled out what seemed to be a guest register and turned to us.
"Sorry for not introducing myself sooner. My name is Rinsha. And your names?"
Yes, this is Master Celica Sylphil, and I am his servant, Shuri.
Servant? Now that you mention it, you are dressed like one.
Yes.
Rinsha writes our names, pen rustling.
So, the room... There's one available. A double?
N-no, not at all. Um, separate rooms...
Rinsha tilts her head at Shuri's flustered reply.
Oh, really? Well, how about rooms next to each other then?
Yes, please.
So, how many nights will you be staying?
Um...
We haven't decided how long, but for now, a week.
Hearing me from behind Shuri, Rinsha is surprised.
Oh, you're a man?
Yeah.
Well, well...
For certain reasons, I have a feminine appearance, so I'm often mistaken for a woman.
Um...
Rinsha eyes me like a rarity. Troubled, Shuri speaks up.
Hm? Oh, right. We take payment upfront. That okay?
Yes, how much will that be?
Two rooms for a week... that will be 140 shillings.
As Shuri opened the money pouch, her hand froze.
What's the matter?
Shillings...?
Right... Ah! Wait, you don't have them?
Yes, we could pay with Rudra until we got here, so...
Come to think of it, when we left Lewinia, Levia said the currency here is different...
Oh, sorry, but Rudra's no good in this town.
I will go exchange it.
No way.
Huh?
Three days ago, the Lewinian army came through. They all exchanged their money, so the exchange vault's bursting with Rudra.
What?!
So yesterday, all the exchange office folks went to other towns to exchange money, and now the place is empty.
No way...
Shuri was flustered. I placed a hand on her shoulder and stepped forward to Rinsha.
Ah, Master...
Can we pay with this?
I casually produced a gem from my inside pocket and held it out.
What's this? Could it be a gem?
It is no wonder she is puzzled. The gem, redder than blood and flawlessly clear, is larger than her wide eyes. It was worth a year of leisurely living, I believe.
You planning to buy the whole inn?
That's not my plan.
Then... I cannot accept such an expensive gem.
Then it is a deposit.
A deposit?
If we leave without paying for the inn, the gem is yours.
So if we pay, you return this gem, right?
That is right.

I get it. Then, instead of just a week,
stay as many days as you like.
Yeah, we'll take you up on that.
Rinsha walked toward the stairs to the second floor.
Um, Master...
What?

Was that all right, Master?
That gem is a valuable gift from the Water Priestess...
Was it?
Yes, worth a lifetime of leisure though...
Master?
Where are you going, Master?

After Rinsha showed me to my room, I confirmed the escape routes and such for emergencies. Finally, I settled in and looked around the room that would be mine for a while. It is a nice, clean room with good sunlight. From its second-floor window, I can overlook the plaza at the center of town. Compared to the cheap inns I used to stay in during my days as a fugitive, it is like heaven and earth... Suddenly, memories of those days resurface in my mind... It was many decades ago. For a certain reason, I once fought a goddess who was said to have vanished into the heavens in ancient times. Against a goddess who possessed what should have been absolute power, I miraculously managed a draw and victory, sealing her will. Then, instead of my own body that suffered fatal wounds in the battle, I survived by seizing the body of that goddess... That... was the beginning of everything...

The god I defeated was an evil god, opposed to the gods who now rule this world. Yet she was still a god. For defeating her and taking her power, the other gods and their followers feared me as the 'God Slayer' and sought to erase my existence. For decades after, my body no longer aged because I had taken the goddess's flesh. I fought and fled from much of the world as my enemy. At last, I allied with the Water Maiden, the sole deity of the great nation Revienia, who belongs to no faction among the many gods, and gained a temporary haven. Over ten years passed... In Revienia, where the Water Maiden is the state religion, attacks on my life by other gods or their followers grew rare. But if my true identity were known in this town, which does not belong to Revienia, all its people would become my enemies, and I would be hunted until I fled back to Revienia.
The room has a lockable chest for luggage and such, so it is clearly a room for long-term stays.

Lost in thought, I suddenly remembered, and from the luggage set beside the bed, I took out a single sheathed short sword. It lacked large decorations, but the moment I held that short sword with its smooth, womanly curves and subdued design, a languid young woman's voice echoed in my head.
(What is this? Finally arrived, have you?)
(Yeah.)

I answer the voice with my thoughts. That voice belongs to the short sword in my hand -- more precisely, it is the voice of the demon god Haishera, sealed within the blade. When I carried out the God Slayer act, she challenged me for that power, but I defeated her and sealed Haishera in the sword I was using at the time. Since then, Haishera has acknowledged me as her master, and as a mighty magic sword, we have fought through countless battles together. However, having lost my power in the previous great war, if I tried to use her now, she would likely seize my mind and our positions would be reversed...
Still, to keep me stuffed away in your luggage like this... is that not rather too cruel?
(Sorry, I forgot.)
(Honestly, Master...)
I sheathed Haishera at my hip and looked around the room once more.
(Hmm, for a frontier town, this is a fine room.)
Haishera, seeing the room through my eyes, uncharacteristically offered praise. Though that was likely only compared to the cheap inns I stay at when Shuri is not with me, like on this trip...
Yeah, it is a nice room.
Hehe, thanks.
I had meant to answer Haishera, but I inadvertently spoke aloud. Rinsha, holding fresh sheets, smiled at me from the doorway.

Come on, put your things down and bring Shuri
to the dining room downstairs. You're hungry, right?
I hadn't noticed until she mentioned it, but come to think of it, I haven't eaten anything since arriving in this town.
Is that all right?
It's fine, I'll put it on your tab.
So saying, she took the gem from her bosom.

Rinsha and I came down the stairs from the second floor. After that, Shuri checked on my room uninvited. She saw the sheets Rinsha was holding and offered to clean the room and make the bed herself. Rinsha initially declined, saying it was too much, but Shuri's pleading look convinced her to agree.
She's a strange one, isn't she...
She must be remembering the delighted smile Shuri wore when she took the sheets. Rinsha speaks to me with a complicated smile.
She's the hardest worker in our home, you know.
Oh, you have other servants too?
Yeah.
Hmm, you keep that many servants? Celica, are you a noble?
No.
Then, what are you?

Without answering her, I sat at a nearby table in the dining room, which had started to empty after lunch. Guessing my silence meant I didn't want to say, Rinsha said nothing and brought a menu from the counter, placing it in front of me.
I guarantee it tastes great!

Rinsha's face lit up with a smile as she puffed
out her ample chest even more.
The aroma of cooking that filled the dining room
was certainly enough to whet my appetite.

Right...
Something not too heavy, and not much of it.
You order like a girl... Then, this one.
Rinsha's finger pointed to a dish on the menu.
I see
So what about Shuri...?
She'll be right down.
No sooner had I spoken than Shuri came down the stairs, her steps quiet but hurried.
Oh, really...
Quiet but hurried footsteps... When Shuri was little, she used to run up to me often. I warned her she might fall and hurt herself, and she's walked like this ever since.
I am sorry to have kept you waiting...
It's no problem, right, Celica?
Yeah.
So, what would you like, Shuri?
Ah, I'll have mine after Master.
Saying that, Shuri stood diagonally behind me.
What is wrong, Shuri?
Rinsha called out to Shuri, looking puzzled.
Yes, I shall serve as your attendant.
Serve...?
Rinsha's stunned gaze turns on me.
Shuri, sit.
But Master...

This is our usual exchange...
Whenever Shuri and I go out to eat,
she always tries to serve like this.
Left to her own devices, she'd do it perfectly,
but while it's fine at the mansion,
in a restaurant it would stand out far too much...
That's right, Shuri. Our food isn't so hard to eat that you need to stand and serve. And besides, it would be a shame to make your master eat all alone, don't you think?
Shuri
Yes, as you wish...
Urged by me, Shuri finally left my side and took her seat with awkward movements. She wasn't reluctant, but rather seemed tense.
I'll have this.
As I looked at Shuri, her face flushed and gaze lowered, I pointed to the dish Rinsha had recommended on the menu.
All right, and for you, Shuri?
Ah, then I will have the same as Master...
Once again, that is a typical Shuri response.
I see...
Rinsha nodded slowly, then lightly elbowed my back and walked off to the kitchen.
Huh?
Soon, Rinsha returned, carrying food for three.
I haven't eaten yet either. Mind if I join you?
With that, she was already setting the table for three.
Sure.
Thanks.
As I answered, Rinsha seated herself across from me with a cheerful smile and immediately launched into a rapid-fire barrage of questions...
So, what brings you two to this town?
Recuperation.

Oh? But I saw you talking with Levia
out front earlier, didn't you?
Does Levia come here often?
Yes, she's a regular lately... And... I thought so...
What do you mean?
So the guy who never showed up, no matter how long she waited... that was you, Celica.
Did Levia say that?
Yes, she was angry, saying 'What do you think the mission is?'
She just told me that.
Rinsha laughed cheerfully.
So, Celica, you came looking for someone too, right?
Half of it is for recuperation.

Oh, so you're not taking it seriously?
Even though Levia is working so hard...
True.
Levia is earnest, but she sometimes overdoes it. I hope that does not backfire on her.
What do you think of Levia's group?
Huh? They're customers.
Rinsha took my sudden question in stride.
Not that... Levia is not well-liked in this town.
Ah, right... Worried?
Yeah.

Hehe, it's fine. When she first arrived,
there seem to have been some issues, but
Levia herself is quite popular with the townsfolk.
Is that so?
Yes, she is. Even with a title like general, she is polite to the townspeople, and most of all she is beautiful, so many admire her, especially the girls.
I see...

It is true that Levia may face resentment from men for becoming a general despite being a woman, but she enjoys immense popularity among women. I often saw her at the Lewinia palace, where noble children would constantly cling to her, leaving her completely at her wit's end.
But...
What?
Seems she doesn't get along with the vigilantes.
Vigilantes?

Yes, they're mercenaries the lord hired when
Levia and her group got here, just in case.

By 'emergency', you mean...
when Levia's group takes over the town?

Right. I keep saying Levia would not do that,
but those vigilantes, hired due to the situation,
are hostile to Levia and her group.
I see...
I finished my meal, tossed the last parsley garnish from my plate into my mouth, and stood up.
Time to work enough so Levia doesn't get mad.

Shuri, who had already finished her meal,
saw me stand up and also rose, looking at me.
Master
I'll be back by evening. Do as you like until then.
Yes, understood.
Shuri answered smoothly, and Rinsha also stood.
Well, I guess I'll get back to work too.
Saying that, she started clearing the dishes.
Take care.
I passed Shuri, who opened the door and bowed, and stepped out into the central plaza. Behind me, I heard her voice as she went back inside the inn.
Rinsha, please let me help you...
(Good grief, she is quite the hard worker...)

A large building stands north of the plaza.
That must be the lord's manor.
The plaza is crowded with people of all kinds. First, I need to go see Levia...
(Where are you going?)
(To Levia's.)

(Oh, that girl...
From what I've been hearing, she seems to be bearing needless burdens again.)

Yeah... I wonder what keeps her in the army
after all that hardship.
(How dense you are, Master...)
(What do you mean?)
Heh, I would not be so crude as to go that far...
(Best hurry. Levia will be cross if you tarry.)
(Yeah...)
Ah, Master, welcome back.
Welcome back... Wait, you just stepped out. Forget something?
No...
What is it, then?
...I'm going.
Have a safe trip, Master.
What a strange kid...

I should not keep Levia waiting.
She'll be angry. Let's hurry to the Lord's Manor.
I headed for the big mansion on the north side of town.
Sorry to keep you waiting.

I was shown into a room in the mansion.
Levia and a tall young man ducked inside.
It has been a while, Celica.
The young man with the narrow eyes and amiable face is Refin. He is Levia's most trusted subordinate, and the only one who can stop Levia when she gets angry with me.
Refin, are you feeling better?
Refin was supposed to have been seriously injured. During the last great war, when fighting a demon unleashed by the enemy, he had risked his own body to keep protecting Levia... But...
Yes, I am completely better now.

His head nearly touched the ceiling. Perhaps bothered by that, Refin stooped slightly and showed me by moving his arm. Maybe due to his massive frame, he recovers quickly. He's so resilient it's hard to believe he's human. I guess there was no need to worry...
Still, don't overdo it.
Levia gently admonished Refin.
Ah, I am sorry.
Levia has a serious and strict side, but outside of battle, she is gentle by nature... but...
Now then, about the investigation results...
She turned to face me. Her look was more than stern; it seemed hostile.
What?
No... nothing.

Levia gave her report in a businesslike manner. In summary: a person resembling Princess Latina, missing for eighteen years, was sighted. She was last seen at an abandoned mine about one kilometer from town.

Therefore, we
will survey the abandoned mine tomorrow...
Levia stopped speaking, and the room fell silent. The report did not seem finished yet, but Levia tried to speak, hesitated, and faltered. ...It seems she has something hard to say.
Levia glared at me.
Ah...
Hm?
Levia blushed and looked away when our eyes met.
W...wait, where are you going?
I have no particular destination, but we are searching for Princess Latina, no?
...The report is not yet finished.
I see. Continue.
The rest?
So?
When I urged her to continue, Levia's face reddened, but not quite in anger. Something felt strange...
General Levia, I will handle the rest of the report. Could you please go check on the soldiers?
Refin, unable to watch Levia any longer, threw her a lifeline. But after a pause, Levia stared straight into my eyes.

No, I will give the report.
About the Princess Latina sighting in this town...
What is it?

Shut up and listen... About Princess Latina...
Night after night, she appears, attacks men,
and, well... drains their essence...
Essence? Like a succubus?
That's right...
A succubus is a type of demon that appears as a woman to men and as a man to women, engaging in nightly intimacies to drain their partner's essence, which is akin to life force.

That's the report. Just be careful
you don't get attacked yourself.

Levia rattled off the rest of her report,
then scurried out of the room, trying to hide
her flushed face.
She's still so naive about that kind of talk...
Indeed.

Left behind by Levia, Refin narrows her already slender eyes in agreement. I suddenly remember the Levia of the past... Over ten years ago, when I was granted a mansion in the royal capital of Lewinia and had just gained a fleeting peace as an ally to the Water Maiden, that was when Levia and Refin appeared before me. Both born to knightly families, Refin admired my strength, while Levia, clad in a white dress with a fleeting smile and white flowers in hand, always stayed by my side, smiling as if to soothe my heart weary from a life on the run. Years passed, and after many battles under my pact with the Water Maiden, when I returned from countless brushes with death, it was Levia who greeted me: no longer in a dress but in armor, sword in place of flowers, and in her eyes a light of resolve instead of her former smile.
Celica?
I shook my head to clear my mind.
Refin stoops to look down at me. She is so tall that in ordinary buildings her head hits the ceiling, so this slightly hunched posture has become a habit, I hear.
This room is probably a guest room in the lords mansion, not the reception room. They sent me here to avoid using the room where the valuables are kept.
Is something wrong, Celica?
I glance around restlessly; Refin watches me with curious eyes (maybe).
No, nothing.

Tell Levia I will also go to the abandoned mine
starting tomorrow.
Yes, understood.
It is reassuring to have you join us, Celica.
See you.
Yes, thank you for your hard work.

As I returned to the Central Plaza, a crowd
had gathered in one corner. From the alley
beyond, I heard a rough, spirited voice of a
woman. It appeared to be a quarrel.
Welcome back, Master.
Oh, you're back already? It's still early for supper.
Have a good trip, Master.
Beyond the crowd is an alley. The fight appears to be happening there, but with too many people, I can't see well from this spot.

The narrow alley is overflowing with onlookers,
and the whole place is in an uproar.

The shop is deserted. Even though it is not
mealtime, there are hardly any customers.
They are probably out watching the fight.

Customers just stopped coming all of a sudden.
I wonder if something happened outside?
There seems to be a fight over there.
A fight? In that alley?
Yeah, that is right.
That girl again...
That girl?
In that alley, there's a girl who's a real hothead.
Oh well. I'll take a break until the customers who went to gawk come back. Shuri, let's have some tea.
Ah, um, Master...
I still have a few things to do. Take a break.
Yes, as you wish.

Shuri and Rinsha are preparing tea.
It would be rude to interrupt.
It must be Shuri who did this. The room is even cleaner than when I first arrived. The luggage that was on the floor has been neatly organized and put away.
From my window, I see a crowd still in the square.
It is still too early to sleep...
I slipped through the crowd of onlookers and made my way to the back alley where a fight was in progress.
What'd you say?! Say that again!

Levia's Lewinian knights glared at a tall woman.
She was a redhead with a long sword, glaring back.
I'll say it as many times as you please! For frontier bumpkins like you to dare speak to us proud knights of Lewinia... know your place!
What?!
At his words, the woman's bloodlust surged. She put her hand on the hilt of her back-sword. Seeing her, the knights grinned and moved to draw.
What are you doing?
Ugh... Celica... Sylphil...

As I thought... Seeing the knights back away when I stepped in, I was certain. Their armor is the same as Levia's subordinates, but these are not her direct subordinates. Levia's own knights, in part because of Levia's character as their commander, all value courtesy, and would never hurl insults at anyone who isn't an enemy. Moreover, they would never address me without an honorific, since I formally saved Levia in the last war. With their arrogant speech and the way they back away at the sight of me, these men were likely temporarily assigned from other units for this mission.
You! Are you protecting that woman?!

Protect her?
I just asked what you were doing.
Tch...

If they can't answer, they know they're at fault. I saw the knights were holding fruit, a local specialty, and the fruit stall owner was watching us anxiously. Most likely, they took the fruit without paying.
Who're you?
The red-haired woman gave me a dubious look.
Just a passerby.
When my gaze and the redhead's finally broke, the knights hid their faces and hurried off.
Woman! I will let you off for today.
What?!

The red-haired woman stepped forward to chase
the knights, who fled with a thug's insult.
But thinking it foolish to pursue, she stopped.
Tch, what the hell...

The fruit seller
"Sorry, Kaura."
Nah, my bad. Couldn't make 'em pay.

The fruit seller
"It is fine. As long as you are safe, Kaura."
...sorry

Right, you said Celica or somethin'. Who are you?
Just a passerby.
I gave the same answer to the same question, and Kaura stared at me suspiciously.
As I silently held her gaze, Kaura abruptly let out a sigh.

Haah... Well, whatever.
Honestly, I figured it'd be dicey with so many.
Anyway, thanks. You saved me.
Kaura gave me a lively smile, unlike before.
No big deal.
Haha, that so? Then I won't worry about it either.
(So this is the feisty girl Rinsha spoke of.)
So it seems...
(She's quite a spirited girl...)
Yeah...
Man, the lackeys of that gilded dame just ran off.
Gilded dame...
(She means Levia, I take it?)
(Probably...)

Seems you knew those guys too.
Maybe you're here to find the princess too?
Yeah
I knew it. So you're a rival to that gilded dame, huh.
No... not really.

Ah, no need to say more.
Their attitude made it clear.
That gilded dame rubbed me wrong from the start...
I run the city watch in this town.
Name's Kaura. If there's somethin' I can do,
just say so. I'll help with anything.

Kaura, who leads the city watch...
The two-handed sword on her back is well-worn, showing considerable skill.

You mean the one who shows up naked at night and attacks men, right?
Levia's report didn't mention nakedness, but if she's draining men's essence, it's not surprising. I nodded to Kaura.
But that ain't human.

My guys ran into it on a night patrol once.
They netted it, but then
it turned to water and slipped through to escape.
(It seems different from a spirit, though...)
And then?

Yeah, they couldn't catch it so they gave chase.
It ran off to Kadra Mine, just outside town.
Kadra Mine...
You're going to the mine?
It's work.
Then be careful. They shut that mine down over ten years ago on account of monsters.
Monsters, huh...
Yeah, near the entrance there ain't much to worry about, but deeper in, I hear there's some real nasty monsters.
Got it. I'll be careful.
Well, anything else you want to ask?
No, not right now.
That so? If you've got questions, just come here.
Here?

Yeah, there's a guard post the watch uses
right nearby, and I'm always around here.

Leaving Kaura, I walked the dusk-shrouded streets
toward the Wild Bull Hoof Inn.
Welcome.

I opened the door. Though it was still early,
the shop was already full. As I stepped inside,
a familiar voice greeted me.
Ah, Master.
Shuri, who had been helping out at the shop, hurried over to me and bowed deeply.
Welcome back, Master.
I'm back.
She looked up again, her eyes gleaming with hope.
What's up?
No, um...
Hm?
Master, would you like to have dinner?
Yeah, I'll eat now.
Yes! Please, have a seat right here.

Shuri led me to a seat. It was different
from the other tables with white tablecloths.
This one was neatly arranged.
Please, sit.
Shuri went ahead to the table, pulled out a chair, and waited for me. ... Well, this is nothing new.
Thanks.
I will prepare it right away.
Shuri gave a graceful bow and then walked lightly into the kitchen.
We stand out...

Indeed, the customers were staring at us curiously.
Then someone stood before me, blocking their gaze.
Heh, welcome back, Celica.
Sorry, Shuri got a little carried away...

Not at all! You're actually helping me out.
Look at the crowd - they're all just a bunch of
lechers who heard there was a cute girl here.

The customers around us laughed at Rinsha's joke.
Most of them really came for Shuri, apparently...
See?
Saying that, Rinsha winked at me.
I see. If it's not a bother, then that's fine.
Of course! Honestly, I should be the one feeling sorry... Are you really okay with Shuri working here?
Let her do what she wants, if you can.
Well, she's a big help, so I don't mind.
Thanks... By the way, what is Shuri doing?
Shuri has been in the kitchen for quite some time.
Ah, Shuri? She was raring to cook your dinner.

I finally understood the meaning of the expression Shuri showed when I entered the inn. Shuri has been working as a servant in my house since she was young, so housework is her hobby, and naturally she can cook as well. But when she is at the Lewinia mansion, cooking is the responsibility of others, and on the road during journeys and camping, she cannot show her skills. In the end, it is only in these special situations that she has a chance to cook, so she must be overjoyed... However, if I were to say I ate elsewhere, her disappointment would be as clear as day.
So eating elsewhere is out of the question.
Sorry for the wait.
As we talked, Shuri came out with appetizers.
Here you are.

When I looked at Shuri after she served the appetizers,
I saw a blissful smile spread across her face.
Is something the matter?
No... it's nothing.
Huh?

After dinner, I drank the tea Shuri made.
The taste and tea set were just like at Lewinia.
No wonder her luggage was so heavy... Clink.
Seeing I finished, Shuri cleared the cups.
Shuri.
Yes.
Shuri responded to my call at once.
Rest for today.
...Yes, understood.
Shuri hesitated, then bowed, tea things in hand.
Good night, Master.

Shuri bowed deeply once more, then silently left. I lay on the bed to review the day's news. My ally, the Water Priestess, wants me to find a princess lost eighteen years... She preys on men at night, draining them before returning to a mine. Levia, with her knights, is after Princess Ratina. Tomorrow she'll explore the monster-filled mine. I'll do the same and head there... I meant this job as rest, but it's not simple. Lying still, I gently touch my chest... Two soft mounds that a man shouldn't have.

The wounds I suffered in the last great war robbed me of much strength, and my very existence has declined to a mortal level... As a result, my body is being eroded by the goddess who originally owned it... A priest of a certain god said this was divine punishment for the great sin of god-slaying I committed.
Sigh...

Without thinking, a sigh escaped my lips... It seems that as my power wanes, my spirit weakens too... Suddenly, the worried face of Shuri comes to mind... I will be undertaking this task while carrying the risk of my own destruction... I hope I do not make that girl, who always worries about me, cry...

Step... step... From the darkness, the sound of someone walking on the earth reaches me. ......Is this... a dream? The footsteps are far too vivid, yet my own existence, hearing them, is vague and formless like mist. Without doing anything, I simply listened to the scene.

The footsteps are followed by a bright girl's voice from the darkness... 'Dad, it's gotten dark, hasn't it.' ... An answering voice: 'Sorry, Alicia. I didn't think it would get this late. Are you scared?'
No, I'm fine, because my dad is here.

The father murmured softly, "I see... A father and child, huh..." Suddenly, a rough voice called out from the darkness: "Oi, there's someone here!" Another answered, "What's this?" The father's voice trembled: "Wh-who are you?!" A sinister laugh echoed: "Heh heh heh... and a cute girl, too..."
Eek! Dad!

The father shouted, "What are you doing to Alicia?!" One of the men sneered, "Heh, we have no use for you." A vicious slash. The father groaned, "Ugh... ugh..." and collapsed with a thud. Had he been cut?
Dad! Daaad...
One of them barked, "Hey, come here." The other chuckled nastily, "Heh heh heh... we are going to have some fun with you."
Noooo...

A goon's voice: "Boss! Let me go first!" Machis retorted: "Idiot! I, Machis-sama, go first naturally." Another grumbled: "Tch..." The many footsteps gradually faded into the distance... The father weakly: "Ugh... Ali...cia..."
...Knock...
Nn...
Knock, knock.
Good morning, Master.
I wake up to Shuri's voice from beyond the door.
Ah... good morning, Shuri.
Perhaps because of a strange dream, my mind was hazy as if wrapped in fog. I shook my head and answered Shuri.
Excuse me.
After confirming that I was awake, Shuri silently opened the door and came in, carrying a basin of water and a towel...

After washing my face and changing into outdoor clothes, Shuri slowly combs my hair.
Swish... Swish...
With practiced movements and careful attention, the sound of the comb gently stroking my hair echoes quietly through the morning room.
Shuri.
Yes, Master.
Starting today, I will be away during the day.
Yes.
Do as you please while I'm out.
Yes, certainly... Um, Master.
What is it?
Please, do not overexert yourself...
...Understood.
Oh, good morning, Celica.
Good morning.
Master, please come this way.

Shuri went ahead and pulled out a chair at the window-side seat. Like yesterday, a white tablecloth covered it, and lace curtains hung only at that window, lending an atmosphere out of place in this dining hall.
Well, it wasn't unexpected.
Hey, what's with the daydreaming?

Pushed by the smiling Rinsha, I take my seat. Immediately Shuri brings breakfast. Freshly baked bread, a light soup, and salad - a simple menu, yet my favorite breakfast is laid out. I would prefer not to stand out, but this was expected ever since I allowed Shuri to accompany me on this journey. I quietly accept Shuri's service and finish eating, then, watching Shuri clear the dishes, I slowly sip my after-meal tea...
Bam! The entrance door burst open, and a man tumbled into the dining hall.
Rando!
Rinsha rushed over to the fallen man, Rando.
Ugh...
Rishika! Go fetch the priest!

Rishika
Y-yes!
At Rinsha's bidding, the serving girl dashes outside.
Celica!
I know.
Even before Rinsha could say anything, I lifted Rando's body from the doorway and laid him on the dining hall floor. On his back was a blade wound, and it seemed quite serious.
Shuri

Yes!
Rinsha, please let me examine him.
Shuri?

After calling to Rinsha, Shuri knelt beside Rando and held her palm over his body. She and I, who possess divine bodies, share not only a master-servant relationship but also that of lord and apostle. An apostle is one who pledges absolute obedience to a god or a similar being, receiving various abilities in return. Shuri chose to become my apostle by her own will, and with the power I granted her, she can use healing magic. However, since I, who granted that power, have lost my original strength, Shuri cannot use great power either...
Ugh...
Shuri's healing magic didn't seem to do much for the wound itself, but it apparently managed to bring Rando around.
Wh-where...
It's my inn. What on earth happened?
Rinsha... Ah! My daughter, my daughter!
Your daughter? What happened to Alicia?
Alicia... I recall the dream from last night.
Alicia... she's been kidnapped!
What?!

So the dream last night was real... I sometimes have dreams like this. The Water Maiden says the ancient god who originally owned this body I gained by slaying a god may be showing them to convey something to me... Just what does it want me to do...?
And who took her?
I don't know... I was attacked near the quarry...
You came here from the quarry with that wound?

I was trying to call for help...
I felt like if I came here, someone would help...

Right, got it.
Tren! Go to the watch and tell them what happened.

Tren
Understood!
At Rinsha's order, the kitchen youth
opened the door and dashed out.
Rishika
Rinsha...
Just then, the serving girl sent to fetch
the priest came back, as if taking her place.

A woman in priestly robes. "This is the one, right?" Following Rishika inside, the woman in priestly robes knelt beside Rando on the floor and immediately began chanting a healing prayer. I placed my hand on Shuri's shoulder, who had been continuously applying healing magic, and pulled her back, supporting her swaying body from fatigue.
I am sorry.
Forget it.
The woman in priestly robes spoke. "It's all right now."

I heard the voice of the priestess performing the healing magic.
Looking, I saw that Rando's wound had almost completely healed.
To complete the healing so swiftly... impressive power indeed.
Mm.
Thank you, Priestess Kuun.
From the priestly robe she wore, I could tell that the priestess called Kuun served Iryun, the renowned healing god.
Oh, it is nothing. But more importantly, what caused this wound?
Yes, well...

While Rando recounted Alicia's kidnapping,
Tren, the kitchen youth, returned from the watch.
So, how did it go with the watch?

Tren
Yes, they plan to send a search party, but...
But... what?

Tren
Well, the watch and the Lewinia soldiers
were arguing. I wondered if it was okay...
Levia and Kaura, huh...
What are they doing...

It's okay, the watch is for emergencies like this,
and maybe the Lewinia soldiers
will help search too, you know.

For an instant, Rando wore a sorrowful look, and
Rinsha cheered him up.
...It cannot be helped.
I'll go.
I seated Shuri on a chair and headed for the door.
Ah, Master...
I stopped Shuri with a hand as she tried to rise to see me off, then opened the door and went outside.

In a corner of the plaza, the back alley with the vigilante station draws a crowd, just like yesterday.
A heavy atmosphere hung over the shop, and as Rando rose to go help Alicia, Rinsha and the others were trying to calm him down.
Thud!
Ugh...

But...
It's okay, the watch will rescue Alicia.
...Ugh... Alicia...

... Understood.

Outside the window, the central plaza looked just like yesterday, with a crowd gathered.

the monsters from the mine could attack the town.

I do not buy it.
What...?

Now then...
Leaving the two to their argument, I left the alley.
H-hey, Celica, please stop!
Refin stops me, looking troubled.
You're good at stopping fights, aren't you?
When it's between women, it's a bit...

Celica

about the knight order herself.
